Lam.3.28-Lam.3.30 are third-person yiqtol with third-person suffixes (יֵשֵׁ֤ב, oshb:Lam.3.28, byte tier); Lam.3.31-Lam.3.33 are three clauses of one conjunction about the Lord (אֲדֹנָֽי, oshb:Lam.3.31, byte tier); Lam.3.34-Lam.3.36 are three lamed-infinitives governed by אֲדֹנָ֖י לֹ֥א רָאָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.36, byte tier). No person, number, speaker or addressee changes across the stated seam, so the ground as written is not carried (tier-1 speaker and addressee marking); what changes is clause type, and the acrostic letter itself produces it - the kaf triplet forces the conjunction openers and the lamed triplet the infinitives - so it is not an independent signal. The onset item is upheld too: the three verbs have no expressed subject anywhere in the span and their nearest antecedent is לַגֶּ֔בֶר (oshb:Lam.3.27, byte tier), one verse behind the onset and undisclosed. Two supporting digits inside that item need correcting, since a reproduced digit with the wrong count-object is itself a defect: the adjacency of divine title immediately followed by the negative stands in 2 verses at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses: Lam.3.36, Lam.3.37) and 3 at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses, adding Lam.2.2, where the hit falls on the ketiv form of a K/Q verse), and it does not reach Lam.3.31 at all, where the negative precedes the title - so the continuity point holds on title-and-negative co-occurrence in both triplets, not on the adjacency figure cited beside it; and the five-verse consonantal figure belongs to the unprefixed string (sweep: 5 verses: Lam.1.16, Lam.3.1, Lam.3.27, Lam.3.35, Lam.3.39), while the prefixed form itself stands in 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, whole-token skeleton tier) - prefix tolerance is a per-length test, never a blind stripper. The classification item is REFINED rather than upheld: the divergence between the span's own literature-type wording and the category's defining content is real, and the stretch at Lam.3.34-Lam.3.39 treats the same divergence as disclosure-worthy while this span does not, an internal inconsistency sitting at an undented high confidence. But the framing that the content falls outside the category overstates it - the ruled vocabulary assigns that category to Lam.3.19-Lam.3.39 by extent, and this span sits wholly inside that stretch - so the cure is a disclosure and a confidence dent, not a category change. The triplet-boundary cut stays permissible; it needs a ground the bytes carry.

The suffix finding stands too: the plural elements of 3:46 are עָלֵ֛ינוּ (preposition plus first-plural) and אֹיְבֵֽינוּ (noun plus first-plural), and of 3:47 לָ֖נוּ (preposition plus first-plural), all byte tier; the section's plural verbal object suffixes stand at וַֽתִּרְדְּפֵ֔נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.43, byte tier) and תְּשִׂימֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.45, byte tier), outside both verses, and the definite 'the plural object suffixes' names a class the row never introduced.
